title: Next Greater Element II
statement:
Given a **circular integer array** A of length N (the next element of A[N-1] is A[0]), return the next greater element for every element in A.

The next greater element of a number x is the first greater number to its traversing-order next in the array, which means you could search circularly to find its next greater number. If it doesn't exist, return -1 for this number.

Solve this using a monotonic stack by virtually doubling the array.
inputFormat:
Line 1: an integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: N space-separated integers on a single line.

examples.explanation: Right of 1 is 2. Right of 2 is none (circularly 1, 1). Right of the last 1 is circularly 2.
Only 4 has no greater element in the whole array.

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ans = [-1] * n
# Write your solution using a stack and a loop over 2*n elements
print(*ans)
